c1.title: Peptide Charge Modulates Ion Binding to EF-Hand Motifs: A Molecular Dynamics Study
c1.snippet: Rare earth elements (REEs), particularly lanthanides (Ln), are of significant interest due to their critical roles in modern technology and medicine. However, their extraction, isolation, and purification remain challenging. Lanmodulin (LanM), a recently discovered EF-hand protein, exhibits high affinity and selectivity for binding Ln3+ ions. This enhanced affinity is partly attributed to the presence of additional acidic residues within its EF-hand metal binding loops. c1.title: Quantum-Guided Binding-Site Engineering of Lanmodulin for Zero-Waste Separation of Critical Rare-Earth Elements
c1.snippet: Rare-earth separation remains energy-intensive and waste-generating, motivating aqueous alternatives for selective lanthanide capture. We report a deterministic computational workflow that couples binding-site engineering of lanmodulin with multireference quantum characterization toward dysprosium prioritization. Four experimentally solved lanmodulin structures were harmonized, residue roles were assigned to preserve the first-shell coordination environment while allowing selected second-sphere and interface positions to mutate, and ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, Rosetta triage, and reduced OpenMM ...

c1.title: Water Layering and Orientation Modulate Lanthanide Hydration in Carbon Nanotubes
c1.snippet: Nanoscale confinement can reorganize water molecules and alter ionic hydration, offering a potential route to separating chemically similar ions. We use molecular dynamics simulations with the MACE-MH-1 foundation machine-learning interatomic potential to investigate the hydration of eight trivalent lanthanide ions (Ln 3+ : La 3+ , Pr 3+ , Nd 3+ , Gd 3+ , Tb 3+ , Dy 3+ , Tm 3+ , and Lu 3+ ) in carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with diameters of 1.09–1.49 nm. c1.title: Investigating Landmodulin's EF Hands in Relation to Lanthanide Recycling Methods
c1.snippet: Rare earth elements (REEs) have distinct and varied electronic properties that have been applied for military and civilian use in electronics, such as cell phones and computer chip technologies. The recycling methods for REEs are complex and require a multitude of resources that prompt new studies to improve REEs separations.
